title: Probabilistic Linear Explanations
summary: The method replaces post-hoc local explainers such as LIME and MAPLE with k-sparse anchored linear explanations over the Boolean hypercube, computed via an exact MIP solver or a polynomial-time IHT approximation. Costs are an external MIP solver or iterative optimization per explanation, sampling around each instance, and the fact that exact relevance-error minimization is NP^PP-hard for neural networks, so only the empirical surrogate is solved. It can fail if the fidelity-error surrogate diverges from true relevance error outside the local distribution, if the chosen sparsity budget k omits features the audience needs, or if per-instance optimization latency is unacceptable in an interactive production path.
rationale: The compute (MIP or IHT on sampled instances) fits constrained infrastructure and the paper claims strictly better constraint satisfaction and relevance error than LIME/MAPLE, but the gain is workload-specific and the intractability caveat warrants small-scale validation before production adoption.

claims.statement: The method replaces post-hoc local explainers such as LIME and MAPLE with k-sparse anchored linear explanations over the Boolean hypercube, computed via an exact MIP solver or a polynomial-time IHT approximation. Costs are an external MIP solver or iterative optimization per explanation, sampling around each instance, and the fact that exact relevance-error minimization is NP^PP-hard for neural networks, so only the empirical surrogate is solved. It can fail if the fidelity-error surrogate diverges from true relevance error outside the local distribution, if the chosen sparsity budget k omits features the audience needs, or if per-instance optimization latency is unacceptable in an interactive production path.
Explanations consistently achieve lower relevance error than LIME and MAPLE while satisfying anchoring and k-sparsity constraints by construction; no numeric factor is reported in the abstract.
